items.title: Cleveland Metroparks Zoo's Primate Forest Opens to the Public
items.summary: After over two years of construction, the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo's new Primate Forest opens Thursday, Oct. 22 at noon. The $60 million, 140,000-square-foot facility houses about 65 species and features new habitats, interactive displays, and a conservation area. Visitors must use a timed ticketing system via QR code to manage entry.

items.title: Cleveland Metroparks Zoo Unveils First Phase of $120 Million Primate Forest
items.summary: The Cleveland Metroparks Zoo opens the first phase of its $120 million Primate Forest project on Oct. 22, giving orangutans a new outdoor habitat for the first time. This is the largest capital improvement in the zoo's history, and the full project will be completed by 2032, transforming the former Rainforest building into a 140,000-square-foot indoor-outdoor campus with three sections. For visitors, the opening adds new experiences like an orangutan-shaped playground, a design lab, a theater, and views into animal healthcare, while also expanding conservation efforts.

items.title: Summit Metro Parks Acquires Historic Quarry Site
items.summary: Summit Metro Parks has acquired the 85-acre former Quarry swimming hole and a portion of the Heritage tree farm in Peninsula for $2.75 million, with assistance from the West Creek Conservancy and a Clean Ohio grant. The property, which includes a rare cold-water creek vital for species like the southern redbelly dace fish, will remain closed to the public for now while officials evaluate its future use, with potential for trails but unlikely reopening for swimming. This acquisition aims to preserve a unique habitat adjacent to the Cuyahoga Valley National Park.
